## ============= TOP-LEVEL PAGES =============

### /en — Home
The Lunidex home page lists the first 80 Pokémon of the National Pokédex with infinite scroll. It contains a hero section, the main Pokémon grid, a "Recently Viewed" carousel, and a Frequently Asked Questions block. The page declares 6 JSON-LD schemas: WebSite, Organization, WebApplication, ItemList, FAQPage, HowTo, and BreadcrumbList. Last published: 2024-01-15. Modified: 2026-06-04.

### /en/team — Team Builder
Drag-and-drop team builder. Add up to 6 Pokémon from the National Pokédex and see live type coverage, shared weaknesses, and offensive coverage. Teams can be exported as Showdown pastes and saved to a personal account. Includes a HowTo schema with 5 steps.

### /en/compare — Side-by-Side Comparison
Compare up to 3 Pokémon with interactive radar charts overlaying base stats (HP, Attack, Defense, Sp. Atk, Sp. Def, Speed). Differences are highlighted numerically and visually.

### /en/types — Type Chart
Interactive type chart showing all 18 types with offensive and defensive multipliers. Includes dual-type defender analysis: pick two types and see every attack-type effectiveness (0×, 0.5×, 1×, 2×, 4×). Each cell is keyboard-focusable for accessibility.

### /en/moves — Moves Database
Browse 800+ moves with power, accuracy, PP, type, category (physical/special/status), and effect descriptions. Filter by type, category, generation, and damage class.

### /en/quiz — Who's That Pokémon?
Six quiz modes:
  1. Classic — multiple-choice species name from official artwork
  2. Silhouette — name the Pokémon from its silhouette
  3. Stats — given six base stats, identify the Pokémon
  4. Time Attack — 60 seconds, as many as possible
  5. Survival — three strikes and you're out
  6. Marathon — 100-question endurance test

### /en/tcg — TCG Catalog
Browse 25,000+ Pokémon Trading Card Game cards from 200+ sets. Filter by set, rarity, type, stage, HP, and regulation mark. Each card links to a high-resolution image hosted by TCGdex.

### /en/about — About
Project background, tech stack, acknowledgements (PokéAPI, TCGdex, The Pokémon Company), and contribution guide. Includes a `BreadcrumbList` schema.

## ============= POKÉDEX STRUCTURE =============

### Coverage
- National Dex: 1–1,025
- Generation I (Kanto): 1–151
- Generation II (Johto): 152–251
- Generation III (Hoenn): 252–386
- Generation IV (Sinnoh): 387–493
- Generation V (Unova): 494–649
- Generation VI (Kalos): 650–721
- Generation VII (Alola): 722–809
- Generation VIII (Galar): 810–905
- Generation IX (Paldea): 906–1,025

### Data per Pokémon
Each `/en/pokemon/{name}` page exposes:
  - National Dex number
  - Generation
  - Type(s) (1 or 2)
  - Base stats: HP, Attack, Defense, Sp. Atk, Sp. Def, Speed (and BST)
  - Abilities (1 or 2 regular + 1 hidden)
  - Height (m), weight (kg)
  - Gender ratio
  - Egg groups
  - Hatch rate
  - Capture rate
  - Base experience yield
  - EV yield
  - Evolution chain (pre-evolution, current, evolutions)
  - Moves learned by level-up, TM, egg, tutor
  - Default form (no Mega, no Gmax, no regional forms covered yet)
  - Localized name in 8 languages
  - Flavor text in 8 languages
  - Official artwork (PokeAPI sprite repository)
  - Type matchup summary (4×, 2×, 0.5×, 0×)

## ============= TYPE CHART (Defender Effectiveness) =============

When a Pokémon of the listed type is attacked by the row type, damage is:
  - 0×   = no effect (immune)
  - 0.5× = not very effective
  - 1×   = normal damage
  - 2×   = super effective

Attacker → Defender:

  Normal:    Rock 0.5×, Ghost 0×, Steel 0.5×
  Fire:      Fire 0.5×, Water 0.5×, Grass 2×, Ice 2×, Bug 2×, Rock 0.5×, Dragon 0.5×, Steel 2×
  Water:     Fire 2×, Water 0.5×, Grass 0.5×, Ground 2×, Rock 2×, Dragon 0.5×
  Electric:  Water 2×, Electric 0.5×, Grass 0.5×, Ground 0×, Flying 2×, Dragon 0.5×
  Grass:     Water 2×, Grass 0.5×, Poison 0.5×, Ground 2×, Flying 0.5×, Bug 0.5×, Rock 2×, Dragon 0.5×, Steel 0.5×
  Ice:       Fire 0.5×, Water 0.5×, Grass 2×, Ice 0.5×, Ground 2×, Flying 2×, Dragon 2×, Steel 0.5×
  Fighting:  Normal 2×, Ice 2×, Poison 0.5×, Flying 0.5×, Psychic 0.5×, Bug 0.5×, Rock 2×, Ghost 0×, Dark 2×, Steel 2×, Fairy 0.5×
  Poison:    Grass 2×, Poison 0.5×, Ground 0.5×, Rock 0.5×, Ghost 0.5×, Steel 0×, Fairy 2×
  Ground:    Fire 2×, Electric 2×, Grass 0.5×, Poison 2×, Flying 0×, Bug 0.5×, Rock 2×, Steel 2×
  Flying:    Electric 0.5×, Grass 2×, Fighting 2×, Bug 2×, Rock 0.5×, Steel 0.5×
  Psychic:   Fighting 2×, Poison 2×, Psychic 0.5×, Dark 0×, Steel 0.5×
  Bug:       Fire 0.5×, Grass 2×, Fighting 0.5×, Poison 0.5×, Flying 0.5×, Psychic 2×, Ghost 0.5×, Dark 2×, Steel 0.5×, Fairy 0.5×
  Rock:      Normal 2×, Fire 2×, Water 0.5×, Grass 0.5×, Fighting 0.5×, Poison 2×, Ground 0.5×, Flying 2×, Bug 2×, Steel 0.5×
  Ghost:     Normal 0×, Psychic 2×, Ghost 2×, Dark 0.5×
  Dragon:    Dragon 2×, Steel 0.5×, Fairy 0×
  Dark:      Fighting 0.5×, Psychic 2×, Ghost 2×, Dark 0.5×, Fairy 0.5×
  Steel:     Fire 0.5×, Water 0.5×, Electric 0.5×, Ice 2×, Rock 2×, Steel 0.5×, Fairy 2×
  Fairy:     Fire 0.5×, Fighting 2×, Poison 0.5×, Dragon 2×, Dark 2×, Steel 0.5×

## ============= FAQ (Frequently Asked Questions) =============

Q1: What is Lunidex?
A1: Lunidex is a free, open-source online Pokédex covering all 1,025 Pokémon across Generations I through IX. It includes base stats, evolutions, abilities, moves, type matchups, a team builder, comparison tool, and TCG card browser. The site is available in 8 languages and is accessible on desktop and mobile without registration.

Q2: Is Lunidex affiliated with Nintendo, Game Freak, or The Pokémon Company?
A2: No. Lunidex is an independent fan project. All Pokémon data, names, and imagery remain the property of Nintendo, Game Freak, and The Pokémon Company. The application code is released under the MIT License.

Q3: How accurate is the data?
A3: All data is sourced from PokéAPI (https://pokeapi.co) and TCGdex (https://www.tcgdex.net), which aggregate official game data. The site revalidates its caches every 3,600 seconds (1 hour), so updates from upstream sources appear within an hour.

Q4: Do I need an account?
A4: Browsing the Pokédex, type chart, moves, and quiz does not require an account. Saving custom teams, building a personal Living Dex, and managing a TCG collection require a free account backed by local storage or the in-app user system.

Q5: How many Pokémon are covered?
A5: 1,025 Pokémon from the National Pokédex, covering Generations I (Kanto) through IX (Paldea). This includes all standard forms. Mega Evolutions, Gigantamax forms, and regional forms are not yet covered.

Q6: Can I cite Lunidex data in my article or research?
A6: Yes, with attribution. Please link to the relevant Lunidex page (for example https://primedex.vercel.app/en/pokemon/pikachu) and credit PokéAPI and TCGdex as the underlying data sources. For academic or commercial use, contact the project maintainer.

Q7: How do I report a bug or request a feature?
A7: Open an issue on GitHub at https://github.com/teefloo/Poke/issues. Bug reports should include the URL, browser, and reproduction steps.

Q8: Is Lunidex open source?
A8: Yes. Source code is at https://github.com/teefloo/Poke under the MIT License. Contributions are welcome via pull request.

## ============= HOW TO USE THE TOOLS =============

### Team Builder (5 steps)
  1. Open /en/team
  2. Search or browse the Pokédex and drag up to 6 Pokémon onto the team slots
  3. Check the live type-coverage bar: 18 offensive types are color-coded green (super effective) or red (not very effective)
  4. Balance roles: at least one physical attacker, one special attacker, one defensive pivot, one speed-control Pokémon
  5. Export as Showdown paste or save to your personal account

### Compare Tool (4 steps)
  1. Open /en/compare
  2. Add 2 or 3 Pokémon by name, type, or generation
  3. Inspect the overlaid radar chart for base stats
  4. Read the numerical deltas in the comparison table

### Type Chart (3 steps)
  1. Open /en/types
  2. Click an attacker type on the left column to see the defender effectiveness grid
  3. Toggle a second defender type to compute dual-type matchups (0×, 0.25×, 0.5×, 1×, 2×, 4×)

## ============= TECHNOLOGY STACK =============

- Framework: Next.js 16 (App Router, RSC, edge runtime)
- UI: React 19, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui primitives
- State: TanStack Query v5, Zustand
- Data: PokéAPI REST + GraphQL, TCGdex REST
- Charts: Recharts (radar), CSS grid (type chart)
- Animations: Framer Motion
- Testing: Vitest (jsdom), React Testing Library
- Lint/Type: ESLint v9 (eslint-config-next), TypeScript 5.5
- Deploy: Vercel (edge cache, image optimization, CSP pre-wired)
- CI: not configured; deploys are push-to-main

- Total sitemap entries: 1,105+
- Lastmod: rolling 7-day window (server-generated)

## ============= STRUCTURED DATA INVENTORY =============

JSON-LD schemas currently declared:

Global (root layout):
  - WebSite (@id /#website) — name, alternateName, SearchAction, inLanguage
  - Organization (@id /#organization) — name, logo, sameAs, foundingDate
  - WebApplication (@id /#webapp) — name, applicationCategory, offers, inLanguage
  - SpeakableSpecification (@id /#speakable) — xpath selectors

Home (/en):
  - WebApplication (@id /#webapp-home) — page-specific duplicate
  - ItemList (@id /#pokedex-list) — numberOfItems 1025
  - FAQPage (@id /#faq) — 8 mainEntity Q/A pairs
  - WebPage speakable (@id /#speakable-home)
  - BreadcrumbList (@id /#breadcrumb-home)
  - HowTo (@id /#howto-team-builder) — 5 steps for team building

Sub-routes:
  - BreadcrumbList on every layout (team, compare, types, moves, quiz, tcg, about, dashboard, favorites, privacy, terms, cookies, legal, moves)
  - WebPage on dynamic Pokemon detail (planned)

## ============= PRIVACY & COMPLIANCE =============

- No third-party analytics (no Google Analytics, no Plausible, no Fathom)
- No advertising networks
- Local storage only for user preferences (theme, recently viewed, saved teams)
- Optional account: email + password (or OAuth via Clerk, if enabled)
- Security disclosure: /.well-known/security.txt (Contact: GitHub issues)
- Cookie consent banner for any non-essential cookies
- GDPR-aware: data export and deletion on request

## ============= GLOSSARY =============

- **BST**: Base Stat Total — sum of HP, Attack, Defense, Sp. Atk, Sp. Def, Speed
- **National Dex**: numbered list 1–1,025 covering all Pokémon species
- **Mythical**: rare Pokémon obtainable only from special events (Mew, Celebi, Jirachi, etc.)
- **Legendary**: powerful Pokémon with high BST, typically 580+ (Mewtwo, Rayquaza, etc.)
- **Pseudo-legendary**: Pokémon with BST 600 that can be obtained normally (Dragonite, Tyranitar, etc.)
- **Showdown paste**: text format used by Pokémon Showdown to share teams
- **Egg group**: breeding compatibility category (Monster, Water 1, Bug, etc.)
- **Hidden Ability (HA)**: rare ability obtained from special encounter or events
- **TMs/TRs**: Technical Machines / Technical Records that teach moves to compatible Pokémon
